findings.title: Published COVID stress figure is look-ahead: '92.4%' is the in-sample kernel replaying the 2020-03-17 label, and it is paired with the wrong day's actual
findings.description: stress_test_date() says it shows the prediction made on the prior trading day (2020-03-13) and compares it with |r_2020-03-16|. The code instead predicts from features AT dt. Those features already contain r_dt (the EWM includes row t), and the result is compared with |r_dt|. The docstring comment 'features AT dt (which use returns up to and including dt-1)' is false. The models are also the in-sample full-sample fits (self.linear_, self.kernel_). With its Scott bandwidth, the NW kernel puts about 100% of its weight on its own training row in crisis regions. So its 'prediction' at 03-16 equals that row's training label |r_03-17|·sqrt(252) = 92.43%. The dashboard hard-codes 'PDV predicted 92.4% ann vol. Actual realised: 202.6%. Error: -110pp'. That 92.4 is the kernel's memorised 03-17 realised move, sitting under an equation for the LINEAR model, and it is compared with 03-16's realised move. The real ex-ante forecast for 03-16 is much lower. The backtest's '91.6% on COVID crash' is also the full-sample (look-ahead-coefficient) linear value; walk-forward gives 108.3% at the 03-16 close.
findings.evidence: Reproduced in the private copy with the pickled model. In-sample kernel self-weight at 2020-03-16 = 0.9999, ESS = 1.00, pred = 0.9242, own label y(03-16) = |r_03-17|·sqrt(252) = 0.9243. The same holds at 03-12/03-13/03-17 (pred == own label). 60 of 4002 rows have self-weight > 0.5 (39 of them in 2020). In-sample kernel R^2 = 0.477 vs walk-forward 0.235. stress_test_date output row 2020-03-16: pred_linear 91.60, pred_kernel 92.42, actual 202.64. Features at 03-16 include r_t = -12.77% (sigma1 jumps 0.932 -> 1.134). Honest forecasts for 03-16 made at the 03-13 close: walk-forward linear 70.0%, in-sample linear 63.9%, naive 70.4%, walk-forward kernel 18.2%. Honest walk-forward-linear error = -132.6pp, not -110pp.
findings.proposed_fix: (1) In stress_test_date, predict |r_dt| from features.iloc[pos-1] (the previous trading row) and label the column with the forecast-origin date. (2) Use walk-forward models: fit on rows whose label is known before the origin, i.e. X.iloc[:pos-1]. Otherwise take walk_forward_predict(...).loc[prev_day]. (3) Replace the hard-coded card in index.html:390-397 with values computed by this function at freeze time. Show the linear model, since the card displays its equation. Today that would read 'forecast at 2020-03-13 close: 70.0% (walk-forward linear); realised 202.6%; error -132.6pp'. (4) Mark the 91.6% in backtest_engine.py/report_generator.py as full-sample coefficients, or recompute it from the per-year walk-forward model. Test: add test_stress_test_uses_prior_day_features. Build a synthetic series with a single 10% return at day k and assert that pred at k does not move when r_k is changed. Also assert that the kernel stress prediction is not equal to y_train at the query row.

findings.title: PDV forecasts E|r| (about 0.66-0.8 sigma), yet it is compared with VIX as the 'implied - realised spread' and drives S1C: half the spread is a units artifact
findings.description: The only target used anywhere is y(t) = |r_{t+1}|·sqrt(252). OLS therefore learns E|r_{t+1}|·sqrt(252), which is sqrt(2/pi)·sigma under normality and about 0.66·sigma on SPX (fat tails). It is not a volatility. Several places treat it as one anyway: the dashboard ('PDV FORECAST (REALISED)' vs VIX, 'Implied - realised spread'), the pdv_iv_spread feature that S1C trades (the backtest's per-year walk-forward PDVLinear uses the same target), and RegimePDV, which uses it as the Merton diffusion sigma. VIX is roughly sqrt(E^Q[variance over 30d]), so the fair realised counterpart is a forward RMS vol. The scale gap is 3 to 4 vol points, the same size as the S1 threshold (0.02). As a result S1C's 'VIX > PDV + 2pp' long-straddle condition is true on almost every day and carries no information. The dashboard's '+6.81pp moderate VRP' is mostly this bias.
findings.evidence: Walk-forward OOS 2012-02-01..2025-11-28 (n=3478): mean PDV forecast 11.19%, mean forward 21d RMS realised vol 14.23% (ratio 1.272; OLS fwd21 = 0.715·pdv + 0.062). SPX E|r|/RMS(r) = 0.660 (sqrt(2/pi) = 0.798). Mean(VIX - PDV) = 6.51pp vs mean(VIX - forward 21d RV) = 3.47pp (the true ex-post VRP). Share of days with PDV - VIX < -0.02 (S1C long-side trigger) = 96.4%; with PDV > VIX + 0.02 = 0.7%. A PDV walk-forward-fit on a correctly-windowed forward 21d RMS target (purged, embargo 20) has mean 14.3% (= realised 14.3%), walk-forward R^2 0.303, mean(VIX - PDV21) = 3.44pp, and the long trigger fires on 63.8% of days. In RegimePDV, mean r_t^2 / sigma_d^2 on R2 days = 1.89.
findings.proposed_fix: Train the forecast that is compared with VIX on a variance-consistent, horizon-matched target: y21(t) = sqrt(252/21 · sum_{i=1..21} r_{t+i}^2) with walk-forward embargo 20. Expose it as PDVModel(horizon=21) once the build_xy window bug is fixed (see pdv-build-xy-horizon-leak). Use it for the dashboard spread and pdv_iv_spread (backtest_engine._build_walkforward_pdv_vol and regime_classifier.build_features). Keep the 1-day |r| model only for the R^2 table. If a 1-day model must be compared with IV, convert it with a fitted scale k = RMS(r)/mean(pred) estimated on training data. Re-run the backtest and update the S1C row in README/dashboard. Tests: assert that mean(pdv_21 walk-forward)/mean(forward 21d RV) lies in [0.9, 1.1] on the real data. Assert that the pdv_iv_spread long-trigger share falls below 80%.

findings.title: Live PDV card says 'vol appears cheap, 1.1th percentile vs 10-year history': 4,125 of 4,189 history rows are NaN; true percentile is about 75th, and the 'history' is a different quantity
findings.description: hist_spread_pp = -rl['pdv_iv_spread']*100 is almost entirely NaN in the shipped parquet. pdv_spread_pct = (hist < cur).mean()*100 counts every NaN as 'not below', so any current value reads as a bottom percentile. The card then shows the blue 'vol appears cheap relative to 10-year history' box. The current spread (+6.81pp) is in fact ABOVE the displayed mean (+4.06pp). The '2015-2025 mean' is the mean of just 64 bot-written rows from 2026-06-22..2026-09-23. Those rows are rv_20d - VIX, because cloud_refresh calls build_features(spx, vix) without a PDV model, not PDV - VIX. The sparkline, labelled as the PDV spread, is also rv_20d - VIX. So current and historical values use different definitions, and the percentile is arithmetically wrong. The published message is inverted.
findings.evidence: The live https://navnoorbawa.me card reads: 'IMPLIED − REALISED SPREAD +6.81pp … 1.1th percentile 2015–2025 mean: +4.06pp ⓘ Spread at 1.1th percentile — vol appears cheap relative to 10-year history'. The parquet has pdv_iv_spread NaN on 4125/4189 rows; the non-NaN range is 2026-06-22..2026-09-23 (64 rows), mean 4.0646 (= displayed +4.06). (s < 6.81).mean() = 0.01146 (= displayed 1.1); among non-NaN rows = 0.75. A local Flask render shows the same behaviour ('1.3th percentile', +8.03pp).
findings.proposed_fix: Build the history from ONE definition: at freeze time, compute the walk-forward PDV series (or the 21d-target series from pdv-units-eabs-vs-vix) against VIX over 2012-today, dropna(), and take percentileofscore(hist, cur) over non-NaN values only. Label the window with its actual date range, derived from hist.index. If there are fewer than 250 valid points, hide the percentile badge. Fix cloud_refresh to pass the PDV forecast into build_features, or stop writing a column named pdv_iv_spread that holds rv_20d - VIX. Test: a unit test on the percentile helper with NaN-padded input (expected 75, not 1.1), plus a freeze-site test asserting that the displayed mean lies between the min and max of the valid history.

findings.title: The PDV forecast on the live site is built from 2025-12-30 features (about 9 months stale), yet it is subtracted from today's VIX. The C21 'flags staleness' fix is never rendered, and nothing rebuilds pdv_model.pkl
findings.description: app.py reads pdv._features.iloc[-1] from the pickle, whose features end 2025-12-30. It combines that with the current VIX to publish 'PDV forecast' and 'spread'. Commit 75b4844 claims the card 'now stamps the feature date and flags staleness'. d['pdv_stale'] is computed (it is True now) but no template references it, so the live card only shows 'Updated: 2025-12-30' with no warning. The repo has no script that fits or saves pdv_model.pkl, and the daily bot never touches it. The model therefore cannot be refreshed or reproduced from the repo, even though CI re-downloads 400 days of SPX every run. The template also hard-codes the coefficients (0.354/0.241/-1.496/0.0346) and the R^2/GARCH figures instead of reading them from the pickle. RegimePDV.forecast() also silently falls back to the last feature row: forecast('2026-09-23') uses 2025-12-30 features, only logs a warning, and returns no feature date. test_forecast_2026_03_24 passes on 3-month-stale features.
findings.evidence: pickle: _features 2010-01-05 -> 2025-12-30 (4022 rows). Its only commit is 64d0e7a. grep finds no PDVModel().fit/save call outside the pdv.py docstring. grep 'pdv_stale' dashboard/templates -> no match. The live card reads 'PDV FORECAST (REALISED) 8.37% … Updated: 2025-12-30' next to VIX 15.18%. Recomputing features from yfinance ^GSPC through 2026-09-23 with the same pickled coefficients gives 9.87% (sigma1 12.55%, sigma2 13.07%) instead of 8.37%, so the spread would be +5.31pp, not +6.81pp. RegimePDV.forecast('2026-09-23') logs '2026-09-23 not in PDV features; using nearest prior date 2025-12-30.'
findings.proposed_fix: (1) In app.py, compute features live from the DB that CI has just refreshed: extract_pdv_features(get_spx_ohlcv(as_of_date=today)['log_return']). Apply the stored coefficients and stamp the date of the last return used. (2) Add scripts/build_pdv_model.py (fit from DB, save pickle plus a JSON of coefficients and metrics), run it in cloud_refresh or monthly, and render coefficients/R^2 from that JSON instead of hard-coding them. (3) Render a visible STALE badge when (vix_date - pdv_date) > 3 sessions, and suppress the spread when stale. (4) RegimePDV.forecast: add 'feature_date' to the result, and raise or flag when the gap exceeds N business days. Tests: a freeze-site test that fails if pdv_date lags regime_date by more than 3 sessions without a rendered 'stale' marker, and a unit test that forecast() returns feature_date.

findings.title: The 'BN-S jump filter' is not a jump test: a single-pair daily ratio with no z-statistic, no tripower quarticity and no significance level flags about 27% of days even under pure diffusion
findings.description: The BNS test (Barndorff-Nielsen & Shephard 2004/2006; Huang & Tauchen 2005) works within day t on M intraday returns. It uses RV = sum r_j^2 and BV = mu1^-2 sum |r_j||r_{j-1}| with mu1 = sqrt(2/pi). The z statistic is RJ/sqrt(theta·max(1, TQ/BV^2)/M), with theta = pi^2/4 + pi - 5 = 0.609, TQ = M·mu_{4/3}^-3 sum |r_j r_{j-1} r_{j-2}|^{4/3}, and mu_{4/3} = 0.8309. The null is rejected at, e.g., 99.9%. compute_bns_ratio instead uses ONE product of consecutive DAILY returns: ratio = 1 - (pi/2)|r_{t-1}|/|r_t|. That only asks whether today's move exceeds 2.24x yesterday's. The pi/2 constant is right, but with M=1 the statistic has no asymptotic justification, and a 0.3 cutoff has a size of about 27%. In the real calibration this noise dominates the 'crash-day tail': 251 of 282 tail days enter only through the BNS flag. The README and article advertise a 'BNS jump filter'.
findings.evidence: Under iid Gaussian returns with no jumps, the simulated flag rate of ratio > 0.3 is 26.72%. Theory: P(|Cauchy| > pi/1.4) = 1 - (2/pi)·atan(2.244) = 26.69%. Real SPX 2010-2025: 28.76% of days flagged. calibrate_jump_tail('2026-03-24'): 'Tail filter (z>2.0 OR bns>0.30) on 874 R2 days → 282 tail days (32.3%) [z-only=22, bns-only=251, both=9]'. Constants checked numerically: pi/2 = 1.5708, theta = 0.6090, mu_4/3 = 0.8309. A causal Lee-Mykland-style daily test (|r_t| / sqrt(trailing 20-day bipower variance strictly before t), alpha = 1%) flags 2.1% under the Gaussian null and 4.2% of SPX days, including 2020-03-09/12/16.
findings.proposed_fix: Only daily data is available, so replace compute_bns_ratio with a Lee & Mykland (2008, RFS) style statistic. Use L_t = r_t / sigma_hat_{t-1} with sigma_hat^2 = (pi/2)·mean(|r_j||r_{j-1}|) over the K = 20 sessions strictly before t. Flag |L_t| above a critical value calibrated by simulation to the nominal size, or the Gumbel critical value. Alternatively, drop the 'BNS' name. If intraday data is ever added, implement the full BNS z-test with TQ and theta = 0.609. Update README/article wording. Tests: under a simulated no-jump GARCH or iid process the flag rate must be within 2x of alpha; an injected 8-sigma return must be flagged.

findings.title: Merton jump MLE lands on its box bounds (lambda = 20.000 tail, 50.000 full). Its lambda comes from an outcome-selected subsample but is applied as an annual rate to every R2 day. The 'expected range' integration test cannot fail
findings.description: The optimum is not interior. Both fits end on the lambda upper bound, and the NLL profile keeps improving well beyond it, so the reported parameters are artefacts of the bounds. The docstring promises lambda = 2-8/yr, mu_j = -3..-8%, sigma_j = 3-6%. It delivers lambda = 20, mu_j = -1.63%, sigma_j = 1.11%. Root causes: (i) sigma_d is an E|r|-scale forecast (see pdv-units-eabs-vs-vix), so the likelihood fills the missing variance with 'jumps'. Even correctly scaled, the mixture acts as a fat-tail scale mixture (lambda -> 180/yr, sigma_j 0.5%) rather than detecting crashes. (ii) The tail filter selects on the outcome (|r_t| via BNS and rv_20d containing r_t). The MLE then estimates P(jump | tail day), and lambda_daily·252 treats every day as a tail day. forecast() applies it to ANY R2 day, which overstates jump variance by about 1/0.323 = 3.1x. (iii) compare_covid_2020 scores against BACKWARD rv_hist_20d, and adding any positive variance to a downward-biased forecast 'improves' MAE. A no-jump rescaling by sqrt(pi/2) beats the jump model. (iv) test_tail_params_in_expected_range asserts lambda <= 20 and sigma_j >= 0.005, which are exactly the box bounds, so it can never fail. It passes with lambda pinned at 20.000.
findings.evidence: Real artifacts, as_of 2026-03-24: tail 'MertonJumpParams(λ=20.000/yr, μ_j=-1.63%, σ_j=1.11%, n_days=282)', full-R2 'λ=50.000/yr, μ_j=-0.57%, σ_j=1.00%'. Full-R2 NLL at fixed (mu, sigma): lambda 10 -> -2545.9, 20 -> -2557.5, 50 -> -2575.9, 100 -> -2583.7, 200 -> -2564.1, so the optimum lies around 100, beyond the bound. With ex-ante sigma_d rescaled to RMS units (k = 1.520) and wide bounds: lambda = 180.3/yr, sigma_j = 0.52%. Tail share = 282/874 = 32.3%. compare_covid_2020 on 88 R2 days: MAE_pdv 14.91%, MAE_jump 14.25%, while PDV·sqrt(pi/2) with no jumps gives 13.15%.
findings.proposed_fix: Estimate jumps on ALL R2 days (no outcome-based selection), using an ex-ante, RMS-scaled diffusion sigma_d(t-1) (see pdv-regime-contemporaneous-sigma). Let lambda be free (bounds of 0 to 252), or reparameterise and report when a bound is active (res.x at a bound -> warning plus a 'bound_active' flag in MertonJumpParams). If a crash-only component is wanted, fit a two-regime mixture, or fit lambda on flagged days and multiply by the flag frequency: lambda_eff = lambda_tail·n_tail/n_R2. Evaluate forecasts against FORWARD realised variance with QLIKE/MSE (Patton 2011), not backward rv20. Replace the vacuous test with assertions that no parameter sits within 1% of a bound, and that recovery on simulated Merton data with lambda=4, mu=-4%, sigma=3% (5000 days) lands within +/-50%.

findings.title: RegimePDV's 'zero look-ahead' claim is false: the diffusion sigma for r_t already contains r_t^2, and the PDV coefficients are full-sample (fit through 2025-12-29)
findings.description: _get_r2_data pairs r_t (r_lag1.shift(-1)) with sigma_PDV(t) = linear_.predict(features at t). Features at t include r_t (the EWM of r^2 includes row t with weight 0.129 for sigma1), so every large return inflates its own diffusion sigma and hides itself from the jump likelihood. The ex-ante diffusion sigma for day t is the forecast made at t-1. Separately, self._pdv.linear_ is the pickled model fit on 2010-2025. Using it for calibrations 'strictly before as_of_date' (e.g. 2020 in compare_covid_2020) uses coefficients estimated on future data. That contradicts the module and method docstrings ('Zero look-ahead', 'Uses ONLY data available strictly before that date'). The regime label R2_t (VVIX at close t) is also contemporaneous with r_t in calibration, while forecast() applies it to r_{t+1}.
findings.evidence: 2020-03-16: sigma_PDV(t) as coded = 91.6% vs ex-ante sigma_PDV(t-1) = 63.9%, with r_t = -12.77%. The standardised return is -2.21 sigma as coded vs -3.17 sigma ex-ante. Walk-forward coefficients at the 2020-03-13 origin give 70.0% vs 63.9% from the full-sample pickle (validate() predictions). R2 days: mean r^2/sigma_d^2 = 1.886 with sigma(t) vs 1.973 with sigma(t-1).
findings.proposed_fix: In _get_r2_data use pdv_vol.shift(1) (the forecast made at the previous close) as sigma_d for r_t. Refit PDVLinear on returns strictly before as_of_date, reusing backtest_engine._build_walkforward_pdv_vol's per-year scheme, instead of self._pdv.linear_. Either correct the docstrings or implement this. Test: a poison test that multiplies all returns after as_of by 10 and asserts calibrate_jump_tail(as_of) is unchanged. It currently changes, because the pickle coefficients would move on refit. Also assert that sigma_d for r_t is invariant to r_t itself.

findings.title: build_xy horizon>1 target covers [t-h+2, t+1] instead of [t+1, t+h] (label leakage), and validate() drops the embargo: horizon-5 R^2 is 0.81 instead of 0.50
findings.description: For horizon h>1, y = sqrt(r2.shift(-1).rolling(h).mean()·252). At row t this averages r^2_{t-h+2..t+1}, so h-1 of the h squared returns are already in the feature information set (sigma1/rv_hist use r up to t). The docstring promises 'realised vol over [t+1, t+horizon]'. The walk-forward embargo is designed for a forward window, and PDVModel.validate() calls walk_forward_predict without horizon=self.horizon, so even that purge is dropped. validate() also prints 'Target: next-day absolute return' whatever the horizon. horizon=1 (the default and the published path) is unaffected. PDVModel(horizon=h) is public API, and the fix for pdv-units-eabs-vs-vix needs a correct multi-day target.
findings.evidence: Synthetic check: one 10% return at position 40 with horizon=5 raises y(t) at t = [39, 40, 41, 42, 43]. A [t+1, t+5] window would raise it at 35..39. Real SPX 2010-2025 walk-forward PDVLinear with horizon=5: buggy target R^2 = 0.8141, correct forward target R^2 = 0.5026. PDVModel(horizon=5).validate() reports linear R^2 0.82, naive 0.562, garch 0.654.
findings.proposed_fix: Set y = np.sqrt(r2.shift(-horizon).rolling(horizon).mean()·annualise); this equals mean r^2_{t+1..t+h}. Pass horizon=self.horizon to all three walk_forward_predict calls in validate(), start oos_mask at train_min_days + horizon - 1, and print the target description from the horizon. Test: the spike test above must raise y exactly at t = k-h..k-1. Also check test_embargo_purges_overlapping_labels with the corrected target.

findings.title: GARCH baseline is one day stale (sigma_t is scored against |r_{t+1}|), and forecast_skill_comparison scores PDV and the baselines on different samples; the article's baseline figures are off
findings.description: GARCH11._sigma2_series[t] = omega + alpha·r_{t-1}^2 + beta·sigma^2_{t-1} is the conditional variance of r_t, known at t-1. predict() returns it on index t, and validate()/forecast_skill_comparison compare it with y(t) = |r_{t+1}|. GARCH is therefore scored as a 2-step forecast against PDV's 1-step. The docstring ('The GARCH forecast for t+1 is the sigma^2(t) value') gets this backwards. The claim that the in-sample GARCH is 'an upper bound on its OOS skill' fails for the same reason. In validate(), the GARCH row is an in-sample fit printed inside the 'WALK-FORWARD VALIDATION RESULTS' table. forecast_skill_comparison scores PDV on the walk-forward OOS 2012-02..2025-12 (n=3498) but naive/EWMA/GARCH on 2010-2025 (n=4002-4021), including the EWMA warm-up. The article's 'RiskMetrics EWMA or a GARCH(1,1) ~0.24' is inaccurate: EWMA is 0.21 and correctly-timed GARCH is 0.25.
findings.evidence: Common OOS sample (n=3498) corr^2: PDV 0.3081, naive rv20 0.2058, EWMA 0.2112, GARCH as coded 0.2316, GARCH with correct timing (omega + alpha·r_t^2 + beta·sigma_t^2) 0.2500. The function as shipped returns naive 0.2004, EWMA 0.2048 and GARCH 0.2262 on mismatched samples. GARCH R^2 in the validate table: 0.1346 as coded vs 0.1571 with correct timing. The relative claim still holds ex-2020: PDV 0.200 vs GARCH 0.132 vs EWMA 0.117.
findings.proposed_fix: Store sigma2_next = omega + alpha·r^2 + beta·sigma2 (the forecast for t+1, indexed at t) and return it from predict(). Fix the docstring. In forecast_skill_comparison, reindex every forecaster to pdv_pred.dropna().index before scoring, and label GARCH 'in-sample'. Better still, walk-forward it: refit yearly. Update the article: 'PDV ~0.31 vs GARCH ~0.25, EWMA ~0.21, 20d RV ~0.21 on the same 2012-2025 OOS sample'. Test: on a simulated GARCH path with known parameters, predict() at t must equal the true sigma_{t+1|t}. forecast_skill_comparison must report the same n for every model.

findings.title: 'Guyon-Lekeufack (2023) … walk-forward R^2 = 0.31' is neither G-L's model nor G-L's target, and 0.31 rests heavily on 2020 (0.19 without it, median yearly 0.16)
findings.description: G-L (Quant. Finance 23(9), 2023) model vol as beta0 + beta1·R1 + beta2·sqrt(R2), with FITTED time-shifted power-law kernels K(tau) = Z^-1 (tau+delta)^-alpha over past returns (t_i <= t). Their targets are the VIX level (test R^2 of about 0.855) and a high-frequency next-day realised vol (test R^2 0.654 for SPX). This project uses fixed EWMA half-lives (5/60/10, never optimised) and scores the extremely noisy single-day |r_{t+1}|. Printing 0.31 next to the G-L citation invites a false comparison, as if the replication reached half of G-L's skill. On G-L's own targets the same features are close to the paper. The pooled 0.31 is also fragile: the top 1% of days contribute 42% of SS_tot, R^2 excluding 2020 is 0.195, the median per-year value is 0.16, and 3 of 14 years are negative. The module docstring also misdescribes G-L as Nadaraya-Watson on EMAs. The relative edge over GARCH/EWMA does survive ex-2020.
findings.evidence: Reproduced headline: walk-forward linear R^2 0.3077, kernel 0.2347, naive 0.0763 (matches the dashboard's hard-coded 0.31/0.23). Single split (train <= 2018, test 2019-2025). Target VIX: TSPL G-L fitted alpha1=2.41, delta1=0.055, alpha2=1.33, delta2=0.025, test R^2 0.888; project EWMA features 0.869. Target next-day Garman-Klass vol (from DB OHLC): TSPL 0.588, project 0.574. Target |r_{t+1}|: TSPL 0.321, project 0.308. Yearly walk-forward R^2: 2012 -0.016, 2017 -0.078, 2022 -0.064, 2020 0.410; ex-2020 0.1946. Sources: arXiv 2406.02319 (4-factor PDV equations), arXiv 2408.02477 (TSPL kernel form), and the SSRN 4174589 abstract as quoted in search snippets (R^2 0.654 SPX RV, 0.855 VIX); SSRN itself returned 403 when fetched.
findings.proposed_fix: README/dashboard: say 'PDV-style linear model (EWMA approximation of Guyon-Lekeufack)'. Report a small table: R^2 vs VIX (same-day), vs next-day Garman-Klass RV, vs |r_{t+1}| (0.31), and ex-2020 / per-year for the latter, all computed at build time into a JSON that the template reads. Optionally add PDVTSPL: fit (alpha1, delta1, alpha2, delta2) by least squares with the betas profiled out by OLS and lags truncated at 500-1000. My script shows this is about 30 lines. Test: a regression test that the reported headline equals compute_metrics on the saved walk-forward predictions (tolerance 5e-3). Add a test that the TSPL kernel weights sum to 1 and only use returns up to t.

findings.title: PDVKernel's 'uniform fallback' can never run: out of support it becomes 1-nearest-neighbour and predicted 18% vol at the COVID peak
findings.description: _gaussian_kernel_weights subtracts log_k.max() before exp. The largest weight is therefore exactly 1, total >= 1, and the 'total < 1e-300 -> uniform' branch is dead code. When a query lies far outside the training cloud (every crisis, since the walk-forward kernel is refit only quarterly), the normalised weights collapse onto the single nearest training row. The prediction becomes that one day's |r_{t+1}|, with no warning. This is why the walk-forward kernel (R^2 0.23, shown on the dashboard) underperforms, and why its crisis predictions are erratic.
findings.evidence: Walk-forward kernel at the 2020-03-13 origin (last refit ending 2020-02-05): query sigma1 = 0.932 vs max training sigma1 = 0.579. The nearest point is 17.8 bandwidths away. ESS = 1/sum w^2 = 1.355, max weight 0.845, prediction 0.182, nearest row 2011-08-11 (y = 0.083). The linear walk-forward model predicted 0.700 on the same day.
findings.proposed_fix: Compute the unnormalised log-kernel minimum distance d_min (in bandwidth units). If d_min > 3-4 or ESS < 10, fall back to the linear model, or widen h adaptively (k-NN bandwidth). Remove the unreachable branch. Refit the kernel whenever the query leaves the training hull. Test: a query 20 bandwidths outside the data must return the fallback, not y_train[argmin]; ESS must be >= a floor.

findings.title: calibrate_jump_mle throws away the best optimum whenever L-BFGS-B reports success=False, and the moment-matching fallback ignores the bounds it was given
findings.description: Only best_result.success is checked. L-BFGS-B often returns success=False, for example ABNORMAL_TERMINATION_IN_LNSRCH, at a perfectly good point. When that happens, the lowest-NLL solution is replaced by _moment_match_fallback, which uses the mean/std of the TOTAL returns as the jump moments and clips lambda to [0.1, 50] even when tail bounds (lambda <= 20) were passed.
findings.evidence: Fat-tailed t(3) sample, 300 days, tail bounds: the optimiser gives λ=20.000, μ_j=0.01%, σ_j=6.10%. The same optimum with success forced to False gives λ=50.000, σ_j=3.48%, which violates the requested λ <= 20. _moment_match_fallback on this data returns (50.0, 2e-05, 0.0348).
findings.proposed_fix: Accept best_result if np.isfinite(best_result.fun), and log res.message when success is False. Make the fallback take the bounds argument and np.clip each parameter into it. Test: monkeypatch minimize to flag success=False and assert that the returned params equal the best x and lie inside the bounds.

findings.title: Several docstrings and labels describe behaviour the code does not have
findings.description:
The following comments and labels are false:
- PDVLinear.fit: 'OLS with non-negativity constraint' (plain lstsq, no constraint).
- GARCH11.fit: 'with analytical gradients' (no jac; finite differences).
- PDVLinear4F: 'VIX is orthogonal to the pure path-dependent features' (the path features explain about 87% of VIX variance OOS).
- Module docstring: G-L 'estimated non-parametrically by Nadaraya-Watson'.
- regime_pdv header: 'C8 Regime - XGBoost 3-way classifier' (labels are now deterministic rule labels) and '1,465 R2 days' (874 before 2026-03-24, 912 total).
- test_regime_pdv header: '42 tests across 10 classes' (actually 61 tests in 13 classes).
- Dashboard 'Model: OLS + GARCH(1,1)' under the forecast (it is OLS only).
- The dead PDVLinear3F/4F branch in app.py would score 4F against rv_hist_20d.shift(-1), a 95%-backward-looking target, on a single 60/40 split it calls 'walk-forward'. Live, it prints 'PDVLinear4F requires VIX column in stored features.'
findings.evidence: Code quotes at the cited lines. A G-L-type regression of VIX on the path features gives test R^2 0.869. grep -c 'def test_' test_regime_pdv.py = 61 and '^class Test' = 13. The live site shows 'Model: OLS + GARCH(1,1)' and 'Active model: PDVLinear3F · PDVLinear4F requires VIX column in stored features.'
findings.proposed_fix: Correct each docstring and label. Delete the dead 3F/4F dashboard branch, or implement it properly: walk-forward, forward target, VIX lagged. Change the card label to 'Model: OLS on EWMA path features'. No numeric change.

findings.title: EWMA features are not burned in: sigma2 starts from a single squared return, and those rows enter the in-sample fit
findings.description: ewm(adjust=False) seeds f2 with r_0^2 (r_0 = 0.31% on 2010-01-05). With a 60-day half-life the seed still carries 79% weight after 20 days, 25% after 120 and 5.6% after 250. build_xy only drops the 20 NaN rows, so about six months of biased sigma2 go into the pickled full-sample fit and into every per-year backtest refit, which also start at the DB's first return.
findings.proposed_fix: Seed the EWMs with the mean of the first 20 r^2, or drop the first ~3·halflife_slow rows (about 180) in build_xy via a burn_in parameter. Test: the features should be insensitive (<1%) to scaling r_0 by 10x after the burn-in.

findings.title: Test gaps: nothing pins the stress-test alignment, the horizon>1 window or GARCH timing; several assertions are vacuous; a fixture triggers a pytest deprecation
findings.description:
All 85 in-scope tests pass while the defects above exist. The gaps:
- No test covers stress_test_date (the source of the published COVID figure), build_xy with horizon>1, or GARCH11.predict timing.
- test_r2_returns_positive_jump_adj asserts only >= 0.
- test_tail_params_in_expected_range restates the bounds.
- test_forecast_2026_03_24 accepts 3-month-stale features.
- The BNS tests check only the [0,1] range and never the size under the null.
- TestIntegration.model is a class-scoped fixture defined as an instance method.
findings.evidence: pytest test_pdv.py test_regime_pdv.py -q: 85 passed, 1 warning. Under pytest 9.1.1: 'PytestRemovedIn10Warning: Class-scoped fixture defined as instance method is deprecated.'
findings.proposed_fix: Add the regression tests listed in the other findings: prior-day stress alignment, spike-window horizon test, GARCH sigma_{t+1|t} equality, BNS size under the null, parameters not at bounds, feature-date staleness. Make the fixture a @classmethod or move it to module scope.

checked_ok: Headline reproduced exactly in a private copy: PDVModel on the DB's SPX log returns 2010-01-05..2025-12-30. Walk-forward R^2: linear 0.3077 (-> 0.31), kernel 0.2347 (-> 0.23), naive 0.0763. Runtime about 10s.

data_store/pdv_model.pkl is reproducible from the DB: the features match extract_pdv_features to within 1e-14, the fitted coefficients are identical (0.354, 0.241, -1.496, 0.0346), and GARCH persistence 0.9789 / beta 0.8897 match the dashboard's 0.979/0.890.
extract_pdv_features has no look-ahead. The EWMs at row t use returns <= t, the same t_i <= t convention as Guyon-Lekeufack, and test_no_lookahead_on_features is a valid proof.
build_xy with horizon=1, the published path: y(t) = |r_{t+1}|·sqrt(252) is aligned correctly (positional shift, so holidays are handled). The abs_r_ann leak column is excluded.

walk_forward_predict: the expanding window, daily refit (linear) and quarterly refit (kernel) are causal. The poison and embargo tests are genuine and non-vacuous. The embargo logic is correct for a true forward window.
compute_metrics: the R^2, MAE and RMSE formulas are correct. Using the test-period mean as the benchmark is conservative.
backtest_engine._build_walkforward_pdv_vol: the per-year refit on returns before Jan-1 has no label leakage, because the last training label is NaN and gets dropped.

merton_log_density is correct: a Poisson-weighted Gaussian mixture with n·mu_j mean and sigma_d^2 + n·sigma_j^2 variance, and log-sum-exp is stable. It integrates to 1, and the annual jump variance lambda(mu_j^2 + sigma_j^2) is correct.
BNS constant: (pi/2) = mu1^-2 with mu1 = sqrt(2/pi) is the right bipower scaling. The defect is the single-pair statistic and the missing test, not the constant.
RegimePDV regime-label and BNS cutoffs are strictly < as_of_date. The cache keys include both thresholds.
PDV's relative edge over the baselines holds ex-2020 (corr^2 PDV 0.200 vs correctly-timed GARCH 0.132 vs EWMA 0.117), so the article's qualitative claim of a modest edge over GARCH/EWMA holds.

A faithful TSPL Guyon-Lekeufack fit on this data reproduces the paper's magnitudes (VIX test R^2 0.888; next-day Garman-Klass RV 0.588). The project's EWMA approximation is close behind (0.869 / 0.574), so the feature engineering is sound. The issue is the target and how the result is labelled.
The in-scope test suite passes in the private copy: 85 passed (test_pdv.py + test_regime_pdv.py).
